info.title: Minds Public API
info.description: OpenAPI 3.1.0 spec for the Minds public API (https://getminds.ai/api/v1 / https://api.getminds.ai/v1). Generate a typed TypeScript client by running an OpenAPI generator (e.g. `openapi-typescript`) against `/_openapi.json`. Auth: send `Authorization: Bearer minds_…_key`; create keys in Settings → API Keys.

parameters.description: API key ID from `GET /v1/api-keys` (cuid: `c` followed by 24 lowercase alphanumerics).

delete.description: Permanently delete one API key owned by the authenticated account. The key stops authenticating immediately (the resolver cache is invalidated on delete). Use this to rotate credentials: create a replacement with `POST /v1/api-keys`, switch your integration over, then revoke the old key. Deleting the key used for the current request is allowed. Requires an active Premium or Team subscription.

Store the `key` immediately; it cannot be retrieved again (`GET /v1/api-keys` returns metadata only). The body is optional: send `{ "name": "prod" }` to label the key, or no body at all for an unnamed key. Requires an active Premium or Team subscription. Accounts whose credentials are managed by an SSO identity link cannot mint API keys.

204.description: The Audience and its orphan-only member Minds were deleted.

404.description: `Audience not found`: the Audience does not exist or the caller is not its owner.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an Audience. Owner only; collaborators and viewers receive 404. The deletion cascades to member Minds that the caller owns and that belong to no other Audience, so those Minds (with their training data and Study links) are removed too. Minds owned by other users, and Minds that are also members of another Audience, are kept. Remove Minds you want to keep with `DELETE /audiences/{audienceId}/members/{mindId}` first, or add them to another Audience.

404.description: `Audience not found`: the Audience does not exist or the caller cannot view it.

get.description: Returns one Audience with its member Minds (each with its cohort profile), the caller's role, the stored grounding, the source bundle (brief, adjustments, keywords, links, files), member-derived baseline distributions, and the transient recalibration state. Use it to inspect an Audience before attaching it to a Study, to poll `calibration.active` after `POST /audiences/{audienceId}/recalibrate`, or to watch member `profileImageUrl` values arrive after `regenerate-images`. Formations are not embedded; list them with `GET /audiences/{audienceId}/formations`. Readable by the owner, direct members, members of the owner's team when the Audience is team-shared, any authenticated caller when the Audience is public, and members of a Study that contains the Audience. Setting `isSharedWithTeam: true` lets every member of the owner's team open the Audience and read and chat with every Mind in it, even when those Minds are not shared individually; it grants no edit rights on the Minds. Explicit Audience members get the same read access. Only collaborators (owner, direct member, team member) receive the sharing fields `isSharedWithTeam`, `isLinkSharingEnabled` and `publicShareId`; public and Study-cascade viewers get `currentMemberRole: public_viewer`, and uploaded-file URLs in `sources` and `grounding.sources` are redacted for them.

404.description: `Audience not found`: the Audience does not exist or the caller has no edit access (public and Study-link viewers included).

put.summary: Update an Audience name and sharing settings
put.description: Renames an Audience and optionally changes its visibility. `name` is required on every call; `isPublic` and `isSharedWithTeam` are applied only when sent as booleans and left unchanged otherwise. `isLinkSharingEnabled` cannot be changed here (it is echoed in the response). Allowed for collaborators: the owner, direct members, and members of the owner's team when the Audience is team-shared. Public and Study-link viewers receive 404. Setting `isSharedWithTeam: true` lets every member of the owner's team open the Audience and read and chat with every Mind in it, even when those Minds are not shared individually; it grants no edit rights on the Minds. Explicit Audience members get the same read access. Setting `isPublic: true` lists the Audience in the marketplace and queues a cover image for it.

isPublic.description: List the Audience publicly. Anyone signed in can then open it and its Minds.

isSharedWithTeam.description: Share with every member of the owner's team. Grants read-and-chat access to all member Minds; no edit rights on the Minds.

get.summary: Get a Formation with its subgroups and members
get.description: Returns one Formation: build status, live build progress, the stored hypothesis, and the real subgroups with their member assignments and confidences. Poll this after `POST /formations`, `POST /formations/preview` acceptance, or `recompute` until `status` is `ready` or `failed`; while `building`, `subgroups` may be empty and `hypothesis.subgroups` describes the proposed buckets. Visible to any Audience viewer for shared Formations and to the creator for private ones.

status.description: Usually `building`; already terminal when the build ran inline.

400.description: `Audience ID is required`, `Invalid audience ID format`, `Formation ID is required`, or `Invalid formation ID format`.

404.description: `Formation not found`: the Audience is not viewable, or the Formation does not exist, is deleted, or is not mutable by the caller.

post.summary: Re-sort the current members into an existing Formation
post.description: Re-classifies the Audience's current members against the Formation's stored hypothesis and swaps the subgroups in place, without a new preview. Use it after members were added or recalibrated, or to recover a Formation stuck in `building` or `failed`. Flips `status` to `building` and returns immediately; poll `GET /audiences/{audienceId}/formations/{formationId}`. Same mutability rules as delete: collaborators for shared Formations, creators for private ones.

404.description: `Formation not found`: the Audience does not exist or the caller cannot view it (the message deliberately does not reveal which).

get.summary: List the Formations of an Audience
get.description: Lists the Formations (persisted segmentations) visible to the caller on an Audience: shared Formations plus the caller's own private ones, newest first, each with its subgroups and membership counts. Soft-deleted Formations are excluded. Anyone who can view the Audience may call this. Opening the list also seeds the canonical default and grounding-derived Formations for collaborators and re-queues stalled builds, so rows may come back with `status: building`; poll `GET /audiences/{audienceId}/formations/{formationId}` until they are `ready` or `failed`. Only one row per auto dimension is returned (ready preferred over building over failed).

200.description: The Formation was created and its build queued.

400.description: `Invalid hypothesis` (needs `intent` and 2 to 15 subgroups with `id`, `label`, `definition`), `Audience has no members to categorize`, `FORMATION_CAP` (more than 1000 members), `Audience ID is required`, or `Invalid audience ID format`.

404.description: `Formation not found`: the Audience does not exist or the caller cannot view it.

post.summary: Create a Formation from an accepted hypothesis
post.description: Creates a Formation from a hypothesis (the subgroup proposal returned by `POST /audiences/{audienceId}/formations/preview`, optionally edited) and starts sorting the Audience's members into its subgroups. Returns immediately with `status: building`; poll `GET /audiences/{audienceId}/formations/{formationId}` until `ready` or `failed`. When the build runs inline the returned status may already be terminal. Any Audience viewer may create a Formation: collaborators create `shared` Formations, other viewers create ones private to themselves. The Audience must have at least one member and at most 1000.

post.summary: Propose Formation subgroups without creating anything
post.description: Asks the model to propose a subgroup hypothesis for this Audience from a free-text request (e.g. "split by purchase frequency"). Nothing is persisted; pass the returned hypothesis (edited if you like) to `POST /audiences/{audienceId}/formations` to build it, or re-post with `priorHypothesis` set to the previous proposal to request a rework. Any Audience viewer may call this. Send `Accept: application/json` to receive one JSON document; otherwise the response is a newline-delimited JSON stream (`application/x-ndjson`) of `{ type, data }` events in the order `meta`, `status`, `subgroups`, `done`, with failures reported in-band as `{ type: "error", error }` followed by `done`.

userInput.description: What to split by. Defaults to "Split this audience into meaningful subgroups."

priorHypothesis.description: The previous proposal when asking for a rework; invalid values are ignored.

post.description: Adds one Mind (`mindId`) or several Minds (`mindIds`) to an Audience. Owner only; collaborators and viewers receive 404. Every Mind must be owned by the caller or public, otherwise nothing is added. Minds that are already members are ignored, so the call is idempotent; `added` reports the number of distinct IDs in the request, not the number of new memberships. Newly added Minds are sorted into the Audience's ready Formations in the background, and default Formations are seeded if the Audience had none. Use `mindIds` rather than the retired `mindId`/`mindIds` fields.

post.summary: Recalibrate an Audience's grounding and members
post.description: Refreshes the stored grounding of a saved Audience and re-allocates its members to the resulting distributions. Owner only. Two modes: research mode (default) re-runs deep research from the persisted brief, every earlier adjustment and the optional `instruction`, `sources` and `requestedDistribution`, or from `query` as a full override; selection mode (`distributions` present) skips research and only replaces the active distribution set, keeping the stored sources and review universe. In research mode the instruction is classified first: an adjustment ("make men 40%", "now they are all vegan", "only 50 to 60 years old") re-allocates the existing roster and rebuilds or evolves the members whose new segment contradicts who they are, while an additive instruction ("and now add 10 African consumers") keeps the existing members untouched and creates new ones within the plan's member cap. The request is synchronous for the grounding and the roster change; member retraining continues in the background. Poll `GET /audiences/{audienceId}/progress` for per-member training and `GET /audiences/{audienceId}` for `calibration.active`. Only one recalibration may run per Audience at a time. Because recalibration rewrites the members' profiles and knowledge globally, it is refused with 409 `AUDIENCE_MINDS_SHARED` when members also belong to other Audiences unless `allowSharedMinds: true` is sent (additive runs are exempt).

query.description: Research mode. Full override of the research query; the persisted brief and adjustments are ignored and nothing is persisted for replay.

instruction.description: Research mode. Adjustment appended to the replayed brief, e.g. "add an income distribution" or "skew younger". Persisted so later recalibrations replay it (additive instructions are stored declaratively).

requestedDistribution.description: Research mode. Topic of exactly one distribution to add. Guaranteed to materialise (as an assumed-evidence axis when research finds no data); the existing axes and targets are preserved.

sources.description: Research mode. Extra user sources, persisted to the Audience's source bundle and cited by the research run. Each list holds at most 20 entries.

url.description: URL of an already uploaded file.

distributions.description: Selection mode. The complete active distribution set after a select/deselect edit of the saved review universe. Presence of this field (even empty) selects selection mode.

allowSharedMinds.description: Accept that members shared with other Audiences are rewritten there too. Required to proceed when the 409 `AUDIENCE_MINDS_SHARED` refusal was returned.

And now add 10 consumers from Nigeria

post.summary: Queue profile-image generation for the Minds in an Audience
post.description: Bulk-enqueues portrait generation for the member Minds of an Audience. Owner only. By default only members without a `profileImageUrl` are queued; `force: true` clears and regenerates existing portraits too. Fire-and-forget: the response returns as soon as the jobs are queued, and images arrive asynchronously; poll `GET /audiences/{audienceId}` (member `profileImageUrl`) or `GET /minds/{mindId}`. Use `dry: true` to see what would be queued without queuing anything.

force.description: Regenerate even for Minds that already have a portrait (their current URL is cleared first).

limit.description: Cap the number of Minds queued in this call (oldest members first). No cap by default.

parameters.description: Return 202 after durable admission and run the complete build on the processor.

422.description: No personas could be derived from the brief.

post.summary: Create a grounded audience from a brief
post.description: Create one Audience from a free-text brief. Attached research files use the same extended screener/questionnaire analysis as the in-app New Audience flow, including Study roles, screening and quota rules, review distributions, and grounding provenance. Public bearer-authenticated V1 requests return `202 Accepted`; poll the returned status URL until the durable processor operation completes.

text.description: Free-text brief describing the audience or population to represent.

name.description: Optional audience name override. When omitted, the server names the audience from the brief or detected personas.

files.description: Already-uploaded research files analyzed through the same extended Audience study-ingestion path as the in-app New Audience uploader.

links.description: URLs to scrape for additional context.

keywords.description: Search keywords used as extra context and research seeds.

includeWebSearch.description: When false, skips Exa search/extraction completely and grounds only on the supplied brief, files, links, keywords, and structurally parsed respondent data.

isLinkSharingEnabled.description: Enable public link sharing for the created audience.

generateImages.description: Generate AI profile images and an audience cover asynchronously. Pass false to keep fallback visuals and avoid all image-model calls for this creation.

trainMembers.description: Deprecated; omit it. Every member of every Audience is individually trained in the background, including large reviewed-dataset cohorts (> 40 Minds), through the same per-member pipeline the in-app flow uses, keeping each Mind's deterministic cohort profile and the request locale. `true` is accepted as a no-op; `false` is rejected with 400 `TRAIN_MEMBERS_OPT_OUT_REMOVED` (it used to create untrained Minds with an empty system prompt that reported ready). Cost and time: each member consumes one Mind training (research, knowledge and prompt generation); a 100-Mind cohort typically finishes over tens of minutes to a few hours, staggered per Audience. The response returns as soon as the Audience exists; poll GET /api/v1/minds/{mindId}/training per member (or the Audience progress endpoint) and wait for every member to report readyToChat before running a Study — Study runs refuse Audiences with untrained members.

idempotencyKey.description: Retry-safety key (same semantics as the `Idempotency-Key` header, which wins when both are sent). Reusing the key within 6 hours replays the audience it created instead of duplicating it.

async.description: Optional async hint for internal cookie-authenticated callers. Public bearer-authenticated V1 requests are always enqueued and return a pollable 202 operation.

groundingPreview.description: Review the quota axes before any Mind exists. When true the request runs research grounding plus a deterministic allocation preview and returns the reviewed grounding, checksum, effective cohortAllocation audit, flags, and size without creating an Audience or Minds or consuming generation allowance. Fresh public previews always return a durable 202 operation, including when `async` is omitted or false. Saved-snapshot previews may return inline; send `async: true` or `Prefer: respond-async` to queue those too. Poll its status URL for the same preview result. Explicit allocation targets that cannot match the grounded axes fail closed with 422, just like creation. Axes that measure the Study outcome itself are demoted to supplementary context and listed in `flaggedDistributions`.

reviewedGroundingJson.description: Exact reviewed grounding snapshot returned by a prior preview. Send it unchanged with reviewedGroundingSha256 to re-preview revised exclusions/allocation options against the same evidence, or to create from the latest accepted preview without rerunning grounding research.

reviewedGroundingSha256.description: SHA-256 returned with reviewedGroundingJson. Both fields are required together; creation fails before materialisation when the checksum does not match.

excludeDistributions.description: Exact axis names whose composition quotas should be removed. Age remains as one eligibility range without within-range shares; explicit gender membership remains enforced. Include required eligibility axes in cohortAllocation.distributionNames. Original evidence stays in reviewDistributions.

memberCount.description: Exact number of Minds to create. Wins over any count parsed from `text` and over grounding suggestions, while remaining subject to the effective plan and creation-mode caps.

audienceCreationMode.description: Deprecated alias for `audienceCreationMode`. If both fields are supplied, their values must match.

datasetSegmentation.description: Reviewed research-variable roles, distributions, privacy-safe pairwise relationships, and deterministic dependencies (recodes and questionnaire routing filters) returned by the segmentation-preview endpoint. Pass `functionalDependencies` and `dependencyDiscovery` through unchanged: the first are hard constraints, so a synthetic respondent never breaks a recode and a filtered question stays unanswered at the source rate; the second reports which discovery bounds applied and is echoed into `cohortAllocation.audit.jointConsistency`. Omitting it does not disable enforcement, but the audit will say the bounds are unknown. Requires Team plus `benchmark_depth`. Structural variables shape a representative cohort; outcomes remain held out and observed joint combinations remain audit evidence rather than respondent-like Minds.

cohortAllocation.description: Deterministic allocation controls. Grounded marginals are converted into exact integer quotas server-side; the LLM does not decide proportions. Omit for deterministic defaults.

targetOverrides.description: Partial or full target-percentage overrides. Unspecified segments keep their source percentages; the audit preserves sourcePct and normalizedTargetPct separately.

get.summary: Audience creation limits for the authenticated account
get.description: Return the Audience size ceilings that apply to this account: the per-Audience plan cap (including a configured team override), the absolute system limit, the custom-size maximum, and per-creation-mode ceilings. scope identifies the authenticated user and entitlement team; allowance identifies the plan default, team override or legacy unlimited conversion; checkedAt is the observation time. These are per-Audience sizes, not a total workspace allowance or remaining credits. Match scope to the intended account before attributing these limits to it. Call this before creating an Audience to learn the real limits rather than discovering them from a 403. Mode ceilings come in two kinds and they are not interchangeable: `automaticSizingCeiling` bounds the size the server picks when no memberCount is given, while `explicitCountCeiling` bounds a size you state — only "balanced" enforces one, as 403 MODE_CAP.

isAuxiliary.description: True for the catch-all bucket (e.g. Other or Unanswered).

memberships.description: Minds assigned to this subgroup. A Mind may appear in several subgroups when overlap is allowed.

status.description: Build state. Subgroup memberships are only populated once `ready`.

dimensionKey.description: Set on auto-seeded Formations (e.g. `age`, `gender`, or `grounding:<axis>` for grounding-derived splits); null for user-created ones.

visibility.description: `shared` Formations are visible to every Audience viewer; `viewer_private` ones only to their creator.

canMutate.description: Whether the caller may recompute or delete this Formation.

isAuxiliary.description: True for the catch-all bucket (e.g. Other or Unanswered).

memberships.description: Number of Minds in this subgroup.

FormationHypothesis.description: A proposed split of the Audience into 2 to 15 subgroups.

intent.description: One line restating the split, e.g. "Audience by gender".

definition.description: One-sentence decision rule for membership in this subgroup.

PlanLimitError.description: Error body of a plan-limit refusal (HTTP 403).

statusMessage.description: Human-readable message naming the plan and the limit.

limitType.description: Which cap was hit, e.g. `audienceMembers` or `minds` (legacy responses may say `audienceMembers`).

requested.description: How many units this request asked for.

itemsToCreate.description: Bulk-create size that pushed the request over the cap.

periodEnd.description: End of the metering window when the cap is periodic.

audienceCreationMode.description: The EFFECTIVE creation mode applied by the server (after the plan gate — may differ from the requested mode on non-Team plans).

replayed.description: Present and true only on an idempotent replay (200): the audience was created by an earlier request with the same idempotency key.

oneOf.description: Per-Mind background training enqueued for this creation. Every creation path trains every member; `queuedMemberCount` reports what actually reached the queue, so a value below `mindCount` means some members were not queued and must be retrained. Null on idempotent replays (training bookkeeping is not persisted).

pollUrlTemplate.description: Substitute each member id to poll its training progress, e.g. /api/v1/minds/{mindId}/training.

cohortAllocationCoverage.description: Which members the deterministic cohort allocation actually covered. Members flagged as real people are excluded individually (they cannot be given an invented demographic profile); `skipReason` explains a null `cohortAllocation`.

reviewDistributions.description: Complete source-identified distribution universe, including screener-excluded, conditional, and unweighted options that were not allocated.

researchStudyAnalysis.description: Canonical content-based classification of uploaded research files and their audience, quota, routing, and evidence contracts.

research.description: Research coverage and axisReconciliation audit. An unavailable or budget_exceeded axis review is not a successful semantic validation; failureReason explains unusable model output or infrastructure failure. `dimensionCoverage.dimensions` lists the standard dimensions covered for this population — the fixed core pool every audience of people carries (age, gender identity, representation, geography, education, employment status, income, household size) plus any the planner judged relevant — each with a reason and a status: `sourced`, `proxy` (wider area or population), `assumed` (model-proposed shares, never used for sizing) or `missing`.

flaggedDistributions.description: Axes demoted to supplementary context because they measure the Study outcome itself (`audienceContext.reason = study_outcome`). Never used for cohort allocation.

segmentRelations.description: Evidence-backed relations from one of this distribution's segments to segments of another distribution of the same audience. subset: every member in segment is in one of targetSegments. excludes: no member in segment is in any of targetSegments. Enforced by cohort allocation and reported in allocationAudit.segmentRelations.

ChatMessageRequest.description: Send `content` (or its alias `message`). Everything else is optional; `model`/`provider`, `response_format`, `tools` and `tool_choice` are validated for every chat shape but only applied on single-Mind chats.

content.description: Message text. Required unless `message` is given.

message.description: Alias for `content`. `message` wins when both are present.

role.description: `user` triggers a reply. `system` stores the text in the transcript as context for later turns and returns immediately without calling the model or counting against message caps.

model.description: Per-message model override for single-Mind chats. Must be one of the supported IDs for `provider` (e.g. `claude-sonnet-5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gemini-3.7-flash`); retired IDs are forwarded to their replacement. Must be sent together with `provider`.

provider.description: Provider of `model`. Must be sent together with `model`. Precedence: request override, then your team's preferred provider, then the product default.

endUserName.description: Display name of the human end user for this turn. Omitted/empty means the Mind addresses the user neutrally (never the API-key owner's name). Aliases: `userDisplayName`, `userName`.

tools.description: User-defined tools (function calling). Calls are returned in `tool_calls` for you to execute; they are never run server-side. Single-Mind chats only.

ChatResponseFormat.description: OpenAI-style structured output request. `json_schema` runs a second extraction pass over the Mind's answer; `json_object` parses the answer as JSON (code fences are stripped). The parsed value is returned in `parsed`; `content` carries the JSON string. Extraction failures are soft: `parsed` is omitted and `content` keeps the prose.

schema.description: JSON Schema for the output object.

name.description: Unique per request. Must not collide with the internal tool names `GET_SPARK_RAG`, `GENERATE_IMAGE`, `WEB_SEARCH`, `DISPLAY_IMAGE`, `GET_IMAGE_DETAILS`, `DOCUMENT_PROCESSING`, `ANALYZE_LINK`.

description.description: When and how the Mind should call the tool. Drives tool selection.

parameters.description: JSON Schema of the arguments. Omit for a no-argument tool.

ChatToolChoice.description: `auto` lets the Mind decide, `required` forces at least one call, `none` disables user tools for this turn, `{ "name": "…" }` forces one specific tool. Ignored when `tools` is empty.

id.description: Echo this back as `tool_call_id` when you send the result.

arguments.description: Arguments generated by the Mind, matching the tool's `parameters` schema.

content.description: The Mind's reply. A JSON string when `response_format` was `json_schema`/`json_object`; may be empty when the turn ended in `tool_calls`.

messageId.description: ID of the persisted assistant message.

parsed.description: Parsed structured output. Present only when `response_format` was given and extraction succeeded.

tool_calls.description: Present only when the Mind called one of your `tools`. Execute them and send the results in a follow-up message.

ChatMultiMindMessageResponse.description: Multi-Mind chat reply: one entry per Mind that spoke this turn, in speaking order.

ChatStudyMessageResponse.description: Study chat reply: the question is classified, every ready Mind answers, and answers are aggregated per Audience.

failedCount.description: Minds whose training failed; retrain them with `POST /v1/minds/{mindId}/retrain`.

ChatCreateRequest.description: Exactly one of `mindId`, `mindIds` or `audienceIds` selects the chat shape. `audienceIds` wins when present; otherwise `mindIds` wins over `mindId`.

responseThread.description: Continue this Mind’s exact Study response with its prior context and assets. Requires one Mind. Repeated creation resumes the existing thread (200).

name.description: Display name. Defaults to "API Chat" for Mind chats and "API Study" for Study chats.

mindIds.description: Two or more Minds for a moderated multi-Mind conversation (duplicates are ignored). A single-element array behaves like `mindId`.

audienceIds.description: Audiences to attach to a Study chat. Every message fans out to all Minds in these Audiences.

minds.description: Minds assigned to the chat. One entry for a 1:1 chat, several for a multi-Mind chat.

mindCount.description: Number of Minds in the Audience at creation time.

ChatPlanLimitError.description: Shape of every 403 plan-limit refusal on the Chat endpoints. `data.code` is always `PLAN_LIMIT`; `limitType` says which cap was hit.

statusMessage.description: Human-readable wall copy, e.g. `Free plan limit reached` or `Free plan monthly synthetic-response limit reached. Upgrade your plan for more responses.`

limitType.description: `flows`: started-Study cap. `messages`: per-chat user-message cap. `responses`: monthly synthetic-response allowance. `audienceMembers`: per-Audience member cap.

current.description: Usage against the cap, when known.

requested.description: Units this request needed (response metering only).

periodEnd.description: When the monthly response allowance resets (response metering only).

context.description: Which surface hit the wall, when the gate knows it.

systemPrompt.description: Full generated system prompt, present only for owners and explicit Mind, shared-team, or private-Audience collaborators.

sourcePolicy.description: Persisted source policy, present only when systemPrompt inspection is authorized.

publicShareId.description: Public share token (present only when link sharing is enabled).

clonedVoiceStatus.description: Voice cloning status; null if not cloned.

trainingStatus.description: Current training lifecycle state, from the same authority as GET /v1/minds/{id}/training. A Mind created from 2026-09-18T21:30:00Z without a system prompt never reports `completed`: it reports `failed` (retryable) until it is retrained. Older Minds keep their historical status. Poll GET /v1/minds/{id}/training for full detail.

readyToChat.description: True only when training has completed; a mind's id exists before it is ready.

UpdateMindRequest.description: All fields are optional, but at least one must be present. Fields of the wrong type are ignored rather than rejected.

type.description: Mind archetype. Case-insensitive; aliases `artist` -> creative and `client` / `consumer` -> user; any other value becomes `creative`.

discipline.description: Area of expertise. An empty string clears it (stored as null).

systemPrompt.description: Replace the full system prompt verbatim (not trimmed). Use `POST /v1/minds/{mindId}/regenerate-prompt` to rebuild it from the knowledge base instead.

sourcePolicy.description: Persisted answer policy. `knowledge_only` always retrieves processed Mind knowledge and fails closed when it cannot support the answer; a request-level setting can never downgrade it. Empty string or null resets to `auto`.

tags.description: Replaces the tag list. Entries are trimmed, non-string and empty entries are dropped, and only the first 20 are kept.

isPublic.description: Accepted for backward compatibility but always stored as false. Individual Minds cannot be made public; share an Audience instead.

isLinkSharingEnabled.description: true keeps or generates a `publicShareId` so the Mind is readable via its share link; false clears it.

profileImageUrl.description: Avatar URL stored as given (not downloaded or re-hosted). An empty string clears the image.

messages.description: Conversation in chronological order, ending with a `user` message. Omit or send `[]` for the greeting bootstrap. With `sourcePolicy: "knowledge_only"` only the last `user` message is sent to the model.

responseMode.description: `sync` buffers the whole reply into one JSON response. `stream` answers with `text/event-stream` and delivers the same payload in a terminal `result` frame; use it whenever generation may exceed ~60 s (web search, large attachments).

model.description: Model override, e.g. `claude-sonnet-5`, `gpt-5.4`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `gemini-3.7-flash`. Provider is auto-detected from the `claude-`, `gemini-`, `gpt-`/`o1`/`o3`/`o4`/`chatgpt-` prefixes; retired IDs are forwarded to their replacement. Without an override the team's preferred provider (if any) or the product default is used.

modelConnection.description: Explicit verified team connection. Cannot be combined with model/provider. Requires streaming, and tools/structured capabilities when used. Errors never fall back to a native model.

provider.description: Provider of `model`. Required only when the provider cannot be auto-detected from the model name.

language.description: Reply language hint. Falls back to the `x-locale` header, then `en`. Strong personas may still answer in their native language.

endUserName.description: Display name of the human end user. Omitted/empty means the Mind addresses the user neutrally and never infers the API-key owner's name. Aliases: `userDisplayName`, `userName`.

sourcePolicy.description: `auto` lets the Mind use its knowledge, web search, link analysis and attachments. `knowledge_only` is fail-closed: it retrieves the Mind's processed knowledge for the last user message, disables every internal and user tool, rejects attachments, and answers from persona only when nothing relevant is found (recorded in `metadata.knowledgeRetrieval.status: "fallback"`). A Mind saved with `knowledge_only` can never be downgraded per request. `request_only` is accepted for parity with Study runs and behaves like `auto` here.

citationMarkers.description: `inline` leaves `[[CITE:n]]` markers (0-based indexes into `metadata.ragCitations`) after grounded claims in `content`. `none` strips them; `metadata.ragCitations` still lists the sources.

tools.description: User-defined tools. Calls are returned in `tool_calls`; execute them yourself and send the result back as a `tool` message. Ignored with `sourcePolicy: "knowledge_only"`.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Accepted for OpenAI compatibility. Advisory only: the runtime does not currently constrain how many tool calls a turn may contain.

participants.description: Names of other participants when the Mind is one voice in a wider conversation. When non-empty the Mind answers in multi-participant mode instead of 1:1 interview mode.

content.description: Message text. Must be a non-empty string for `user` (whitespace-only is rejected with 400); may be empty for `assistant`. An array of content parts (`{ type: "text", text }`) is also accepted.

tool_calls.description: On `assistant` messages: the tool calls the Mind made in that turn, echoed back verbatim.

tool_call_id.description: On `tool` messages: the `id` of the call this result answers. `content` is the tool result (typically a JSON string).

attachedFiles.description: Files, images or web pages to process (PDF, DOCX, TXT/MD, CSV/XLSX, PNG/JPG/WEBP, HTML). Processed in parallel (30 s per file) before the Mind sees the message; the extracted content is appended to the last user message but never persisted. Attachments are deduplicated by `url` across the whole history. Not allowed with `sourcePolicy: "knowledge_only"`.

MindCompletionAttachment.description: Provide either `url` or `path`, not both. Files without a resolvable `url` are skipped.

url.description: Public HTTP(S) URL of the file or web page.

path.description: Supabase storage path of an uploaded file (signed automatically).

name.description: Display name shown to the Mind.

messageId.description: Opaque per-call ID (`msg_` + 32 hex chars). Nothing is persisted; use it for your own correlation.

content.description: The Mind's reply. A JSON string when `response_format` was `json_schema`/`json_object`; empty when the turn ended in `tool_calls` or an image-only result.

parsed.description: Parsed structured output. Present only when `response_format` was given and extraction succeeded.

tool_calls.description: Present only when the Mind called one of your `tools`.

MindCompletionMetadata.description: Present only when at least one field applies. Internal tools (knowledge retrieval, web search, image display/generation, link analysis, document processing) surface their results here, never in `tool_calls`.

ragCitations.description: Verified knowledge, web, link and document sources. Inline `[[CITE:n]]` markers in `content` index into this array (0-based).

images.description: Images the Mind displayed or generated. URLs are absolute.

documentAnalysis.description: Analysis text of the last processed attachment, when any.

sourcePolicy.description: Present only for a knowledge-only reply.

displaySource.description: Human-readable source name, file name or URL host.

similarity.description: Relevance score for knowledge and web sources.

source.description: `generated` for AI-generated images, otherwise where the displayed image came from (e.g. `memory`).

MindCompletionKnowledgeRetrieval.description: Source-safe retrieval summary for `sourcePolicy: "knowledge_only"`. Titles only; storage paths and raw file contents are never returned.

status.description: `grounded` when relevant knowledge chunks were used; `fallback` when none matched and the Mind answered from persona/cohort profile only.

retrievalAttempted.description: False when the request had no user question to retrieve for.

chunksFound.description: Chunks used for this answer (not the Mind's total embedding count).

MindCompletionAnswerProvenance.description: Answer-level origin recorded on every reply. Exact claim citations (`ragCitations` + `chatCitationProvenance`) take precedence when present.

unsupported.description: True when a factual question could not be grounded; the Mind was instructed to express uncertainty.

enum: This Mind failed training and must be retrained before it can chat

MindCompletionSseEvent.description: `data` payloads by frame: `start` → MindCompletionStartEvent, `result` → MindCompletionResponse, `error` → MindCompletionErrorEvent, `done` → MindCompletionDoneEvent. Lines starting with `:` are heartbeats and carry no data.

timestamp.description: Unix epoch milliseconds when generation began.

MindCompletionErrorEvent.description: Sent instead of `result` when the completion failed after the stream opened. `status` is the HTTP status the same request would have received in `sync` mode.

status.description: `idle` also covers an unknown or mismatched `jobId` (the job does not belong to this Mind, format, and locale).

mimeType.description: Present for `completed`: `application/pdf`, `text/markdown;charset=utf-8`, or the docx / pptx OpenXML MIME type.

downloadUrl.description: Present for `completed`: relative path to `GET /v1/minds/{mindId}/export-download` for this artifact.

content.description: Inline UTF-8 markdown; present for completed `md` exports unless `metadata=1`.

contentBase64.description: Inline base64 file bytes; present for completed `pdf` / `docx` / `pptx` exports unless `metadata=1`.

KnowledgeItemProcessing.description: Durable background-processing state recorded on the item. `status` is the ingestion lifecycle; poll the item `statusUrl` for embedding/pattern counts and the `readyForRetrieval` gate. Workers may add further keys (for example `error` or `promptRegenerated`).

regeneratePrompt.description: Whether the Mind system prompt is regenerated once embeddings and patterns finish successfully.

error.description: Failure detail when `status` is `failed`, if the worker recorded one.

promptRegenerated.description: Whether the optional prompt-regeneration step completed. Present only when recorded.

KnowledgeItem.description: A knowledge source attached to a Mind. Exactly one of `link` or `filePath` is set for user-added items; auto-collected sources can also be link-based.

description.description: Human-readable description supplied when the item was added.

link.description: Source URL for link-based items; null for uploaded files.

filePath.description: Storage path of the uploaded file (`portfolio/{userId}/{timestamp}_{name}`); null for link-based items.

isWatched.description: True when a link item is watched for weekly content changes (managed in the product UI; links only).

processing.description: Absent for legacy items without recorded processing metadata.

statusUrl.description: Relative path of `GET /api/v1/minds/{mindId}/knowledge/{itemId}/status` for this item.

link.description: URL of a web page, YouTube video, or research paper. Note the field is `link`, not `url`.

regeneratePrompt.description: Regenerate the Mind system prompt once ingestion succeeds.

name.description: Filename including extension; used to derive the storage name and content type.

url.description: Public/signed HTTPS URL, or a Minds workspace upload URL (read directly from storage). Private-network and unsafe URLs are rejected.

type.description: MIME type hint. Falls back to the fetched response `Content-Type`.

regeneratePrompt.description: Regenerate the Mind system prompt once ingestion succeeds.

keywords.description: Search topics. Trimmed, de-duplicated, and capped at 15 (extras are silently dropped). Must contain at least one non-empty string.

regeneratePrompt.description: Regenerate the Mind system prompt after the collected content is processed.

KnowledgeItemAccepted.title: Knowledge item accepted
KnowledgeItemAccepted.description: Created item for file and link modes. `filePath` is present for uploads, `link` for URLs; `isWatched`/`updatedAt` are not included here (see the list endpoint).

statusUrl.description: Relative path of `GET /api/v1/minds/{mindId}/knowledge/{itemId}/status`; poll until `readyForRetrieval` is true.

keywords.description: Normalised keywords actually queued (trimmed, de-duplicated, max 15).

message.example: Knowledge enrichment queued with 2 keyword(s). Web search and content processing will run in background.

mind.description: The extracted pattern text (citation/quote) supporting this sub-aspect.

portfolioItemId.description: Knowledge item the pattern was extracted from. Present only for privileged callers; null for patterns without a source item.

createdAt.description: When the pattern was extracted. Present only for privileged callers.

id.description: Framework sub-aspect ID, or `(none)` for patterns filed directly under the aspect.

name.description: Sub-aspect name, or `(General)` for patterns without a sub-aspect.

description.description: Framework definition; empty string when unknown.

occurrences.description: Number of patterns matched to this sub-aspect.
Number of patterns matched to this aspect (sum of its sub-aspects).

subAspects.description: Sub-aspects with at least one occurrence, sorted by occurrences descending.

totalOccurrences.description: Sum of aspect occurrences within this framework.

aspects.description: Aspects with at least one occurrence, sorted by occurrences descending.

aspect.description: Detected method / aspect (legacy name for the `method` column).

subAspect.description: Detected competency / sub-aspect (legacy name for the `competency` column).

mind.description: The supporting quote or insight text for this pattern.

userId.description: User who owned the source material. Full rows only.

messageId.description: Chat message the pattern was extracted from, if any. Full rows only.

portfolioItemId.description: Knowledge item the pattern was extracted from, if any. Full rows only.

isPredefinedAspect.description: Whether `aspect` comes from a predefined framework. Full rows only.

isPredefinedSubAspect.description: Whether `subAspect` comes from a predefined framework. Full rows only.

readyToChat.description: True only when training has completed and the mind can answer.

retryable.description: When true, POST /v1/minds/{id}/retrain may recover the mind.

sourcePolicy.description: Persisted source policy for this Mind.

profileImageUrl.description: Avatar image; resolved to an absolute URL.

description.description: Short summary. Defaults to "Created via API".

personaContext.description: Required when `mode=clone` (name + brief context of the person to emulate).

contextLink.description: Required when `mode=link` (URL the AI will scrape).

profileImageUrl.description: External avatar URL; downloaded and persisted to Supabase storage.

generateImage.description: Trigger async AI profile-image generation after creation. Defaults to true for auto-training modes; pass false to opt out.

includeWebSearch.description: Set false to skip automatic web research. For a strictly private source-only Mind, use mode=manual, upload knowledge, then regenerate the prompt.

isRealPerson.description: Whether the Mind emulates a real, named person. Defaults to true for mode=clone and false otherwise. Synthetic Minds (false) get name-blind persona prompts: the name is a label, never the seed of the biography.

sourcePolicy.description: Persisted source policy. knowledge_only always retrieves processed Mind knowledge and fails closed when it cannot support the answer.

locale.description: ISO 639-1 code for the auto-generated description language. Falls back to the user's preferredLanguage, then `en`.

question.description: Research question to ask the study.

sourcePolicy.description: knowledge_only forbids live/request sources, requires each Mind's processed knowledge, and fails closed when retrieval is empty.

historyMode.description: How much of each Mind's own prior answers this question carries. Defaults to none. Use last5 when a respondent's coherence across items is the deliverable.

audienceIds.description: Optional subset of attached audience UUIDs to ask. Defaults to all audiences on the study.

attachments.description: Files or images to process once and include as context for every Mind in the Study.

links.description: Web links to fetch and summarize for context.

keywords.description: Keyword/source pairs to fetch and summarize for context.

model.description: Optional per-request model override. Must be sent together with `provider`.

provider.description: Provider for the model override. Must be sent together with `model`.

responseMode.description: Use queued to persist the question and return immediately while durable workers generate the answers.

responseForm.description: How long and how shaped each answer should be, for qualitative questions: `concise` one short message (5-20 words), `standard` 1-3 sentences (25-90 words), `expanded` 2-5 sentences (70-180 words). Omit to let the question decide, which is the existing behaviour. An authored form outranks the phrasing of the question, so a fixed instrument keeps its exact wording. Ignored for scale, categorical and multiselect questions, which are shaped by their answer space.

clientRequestId.description: Optional idempotency key for queued submissions.

url.description: External URL for the uploaded or remote file.

path.description: Storage path for an uploaded file.

url.description: URL to fetch when separate from `label`.
Optional source URL for the keyword.

total.description: Total number of minds that will answer.

responseMode.description: Answer-depth and grounding policy, orthogonal to the structured response type.

citationSources.description: Claim-level sources referenced by zero-based [N] markers in message.

reason.description: Only when status is unavailable: why no sources could be attributed.

origin.description: Canonical answer origin. `group_grounding` was renamed to `audience_grounding`; it is still listed so a response recorded before the rename validates.

originLegacy.description: Pre-rename spelling of `origin`, present only when one exists. Switch to `origin`; this field will be removed.

methodId.description: A registered research method that is currently available. Methods that design their own tasks at execution (Van Westendorp, MaxDiff, Kano, NPS, …) keep only the qualitative questions in `questions`.

canManage.description: Only the owner may update, delete or share this template.

canShareWithTeam.description: The owner has a team, or can turn off existing sharing.

requestId.description: Reuse only for retries of the same save.

isSharedWithTeam.description: Owner only. Share with the authenticated owner’s current team, or turn sharing off.

requestId.description: Unique per intended draft; reuse only for retries.

ApiKeyAuth.description: Personal API key. Format: `Bearer minds_…_key`. Create one at https://getminds.ai/settings/api-keys.
